posts.author: BeanmanBowen
posts.body: I'm making an ability for one of my characters to take on the class of another character mid battle. The problem is i dont know how to store a class ID in a variable or how to change the targets class to that variable. Help would be apreciated, thank you.

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body:
Put this in a Variable OP
Get Class ID from x-th actor in your party:
Code:
$gameParty.members()[x] ? $gameParty.members()[x].currentClass().id : 0
Replace x with the index. Sorry, I don't remember whether you need to type 0 or 1, just try it out.
This call returns 0 when this actor isn't present in your party.
Get Class ID from x-th actor from your database:
Code:
$gameActors.actor(x).currentClass().id
Put this in a Script Call
Set Class from x-th actor in your party by Variable
Code:
$gameParty.members()[x].changeClass($gameVariables.value(1), true)
Set Class from x-th actor from your database
Code:
$gameActors.actor(x).changeClass($gameVariables.value(1), true)

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
BeanmanBowen said:
i cant figure out how to run a common event through a state, searches suggest its impossible, and plugins suggest yanfly but as an MZ dev thats not an option.
Click to expand...
Correct, you can't "run a common event through a state," you'd need to do this through code. Yanfly's plugins are written for MV, but there are MZ plugins which do the same things.
The direct port of Yanfly's plugins for MZ is done by VisuStella, but if you're not already using their products you can do this with my lighter weight
Eval Tags plugin
.
You would give the skill the notetag:
Code:
<Action Apply Eval>
user.origClass = user.currentClass().id;
user.changeClass(target.currentClass().id, true);
// Specify the ID of your state on this line
user.addState(69);
</Action Apply Eval>
replace 69 with the ID of the state which determines how long the effect lasts.
Then, give the state the notetag:
Code:
<State Remove Eval>
user.changeClass(user.origClass, true);
delete user.origClass;
</State Remove Eval>

I suggest you try to un-fixate yourself on common events if you're trying to make the engine do things beyond what it's made to do.
